loading: Reading the objects on the path…
banner: Read from the cluster's objects only: no probe pod is started and no traffic is sent.
stopped: The checks after the broken link were not run.

summary.warn: No broken link found, but some links need attention.
summary.unknown: No broken link found, but some links could not be checked.
summary.ok: No broken link found on the path.

service.externalName: The Service is an alias for {{name}}: cluster DNS answers with a CNAME record to it.
service.externalNameNote: No pods, endpoints or network policies are involved. Sextant does not resolve the name.
service.externalNameEmpty: The ExternalName Service has no externalName: DNS has nothing to answer with.
service.externalNameIp: externalName is the IP address {{name}}: DNS returns it as a CNAME target, which most clients cannot resolve. Use a Service without a selector and an EndpointSlice for an address.
service.externalNameInvalid: externalName {{name}} is not a DNS name (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and dots, without a scheme, port or path).
service.portMissing: Service {{name}} has no port {{port}}. Its ports: {{ports}}.
service.headless: The Service is headless (clusterIP None): DNS returns the addresses of its ready pods, there is no virtual IP.
service.headlessNoPorts: It declares no ports: that is valid for a headless Service with a selector, clients connect to the pod addresses on any port.
service.manual: Service {{name}} has no selector: its endpoints are managed by hand, in EndpointSlices labelled kubernetes.io/service-name={{name}}.
service.manualNoSlices: No EndpointSlice is labelled kubernetes.io/service-name={{name}}: the Service has no endpoints.
service.manualNoReady_one: The EndpointSlices list {{count}} endpoint, and it is not ready.
service.manualNoReady_other: The EndpointSlices list {{count}} endpoints, and none is ready.
service.podsUnknown: The pods of namespace {{namespace}} cannot be read, so the selector cannot be checked.
service.noPods: The selector {{selector}} matches no pod in namespace {{namespace}}.
service.nearMiss_one: {{count}} pod has every label of the selector except {{label}}.
service.nearMiss_other: {{count}} pods have every label of the selector except {{label}}.
service.allTerminating: Every pod the selector matches is terminating.
service.noneReady_one: The selector matches {{count}} pod, and it is not Ready, so it gets no traffic.
service.noneReady_other: The selector matches {{count}} pods, and none is Ready, so none gets traffic.
service.noneReadyPublished_one: {{count}} pod is not Ready, but publishNotReadyAddresses is set: it gets traffic anyway.
service.noneReadyPublished_other: {{count}} pods are not Ready, but publishNotReadyAddresses is set: they get traffic anyway.
service.someReady_one: {{count}} pod of {{total}} is Ready; the others get no traffic.
service.someReady_other: {{count}} pods of {{total}} are Ready; the others get no traffic.
service.namedPortMissing: Port {{port}} targets the container port named {{name}}, and no container of the pods has a port with that name.
service.namedPortProtocol: Port {{port}} targets the container port named {{name}}, and the pods have it only with another protocol than {{protocol}}.
service.namedPortSome_one: Port {{port}} targets the container port named {{name}}: only {{count}} pod of {{total}} has it; the others get no traffic on this port.
service.namedPortSome_other: Port {{port}} targets the container port named {{name}}: only {{count}} pods of {{total}} have it; the others get no traffic on this port.
service.namedPort: Port {{port}} targets the container port named {{name}}, which the pods have: {{targets}}.
service.targetPort: Port {{port}} targets container port {{target}}, which the pods declare.
service.protocolMismatch: Port {{port}} uses {{protocol}}, but the pods declare container port {{target}} only for: {{declared}}.
service.portNotDeclared: Port {{port}} targets container port {{target}}, which no container declares. It still works if the process listens on that port.
service.slicesUnknown: The EndpointSlices of namespace {{namespace}} cannot be read.
service.noSlices: The Service has no EndpointSlice yet, so traffic has nowhere to go. If this lasts, the EndpointSlice controller is not working.
service.slicesNoReady_one: The EndpointSlices list {{count}} endpoint, and it is not ready.
service.slicesNoReady_other: The EndpointSlices list {{count}} endpoints, and none is ready.
service.slicesDiffer_one: The EndpointSlices list {{count}} ready endpoint, while Ready pods: {{pods}}. They usually catch up within seconds.
service.slicesDiffer_other: The EndpointSlices list {{count}} ready endpoints, while Ready pods: {{pods}}. They usually catch up within seconds.
service.slices_one: The EndpointSlices list {{count}} ready endpoint, as expected.
service.slices_other: The EndpointSlices list {{count}} ready endpoints, as expected.
service.clusterIp: The Service is reachable inside the cluster only, as {{name}}.{{namespace}}.svc.
service.nodePorts: Every node takes traffic on node ports: {{ports}}.
service.localPolicy: externalTrafficPolicy is Local: only nodes that run a ready pod answer, and the client's address is kept.
service.lbAddress: The load balancer has an address: {{addresses}}.
service.lbPendingNew: The load balancer has no address yet; the Service was created a few minutes ago.
service.lbPendingMinutes_one: The load balancer has had no address for {{count}} minute.
service.lbPendingMinutes_other: The load balancer has had no address for {{count}} minutes.
service.lbPendingHours_one: The load balancer has had no address for {{count}} hour.
service.lbPendingHours_other: The load balancer has had no address for {{count}} hours.
service.lbPendingWhy: No controller has provisioned a load balancer: the cluster may have none (kind, bare metal without MetalLB), or it failed. The Service's events say why.
service.externalIps: The Service also takes traffic sent to {{addresses}} on ports: {{ports}}.
service.affinity_one: Session affinity ClientIP: requests of one client go to the same pod for {{count}} second.
service.affinity_other: Session affinity ClientIP: requests of one client go to the same pod for {{count}} seconds.

ingress.classUnknown: The IngressClasses cannot be read, so the controller of this Ingress cannot be told.
ingress.classDefault: The Ingress names no class, so the default IngressClass {{name}} applies (controller {{controller}}).
ingress.classMissing: spec.ingressClassName is {{name}}, and no IngressClass has that name: no controller picks the Ingress up.
ingress.classMissingClaimed: spec.ingressClassName is {{name}}, and no IngressClass has that name, but the Ingress has an address: some controller has claimed it. Which one, and whether it runs, cannot be told.
ingress.classAnnotation: The class is set by the deprecated annotation kubernetes.io/ingress.class ({{name}}); use spec.ingressClassName.
ingress.classAnnotationNoObject: The deprecated annotation kubernetes.io/ingress.class names {{name}}, and no IngressClass has that name: only a controller that still reads the annotation picks the Ingress up.
ingress.classManyDefaults: The Ingress names no class, and several IngressClasses are marked default: {{names}}. Name one in spec.ingressClassName.
ingress.classNone: The Ingress names no class and no IngressClass is marked default: no controller picks it up. Set spec.ingressClassName.
ingress.classNoneClaimed: The Ingress names no class and no IngressClass is marked default, but it has an address: some controller that takes Ingresses without a class (such as ingress-nginx with --watch-ingress-without-class, or Traefik) has claimed it. Set spec.ingressClassName to make the choice explicit.
ingress.controllerUnknown: Sextant cannot tell whether controller {{controller}} runs: it does not know how its pods are labelled, and the Ingress has no address.
ingress.controllerByAddress: Controller {{controller}} published an address for the Ingress, so it handles it.
ingress.controllerOutside: Controller {{controller}} configures a load balancer outside the cluster: traffic reaches the pods from that load balancer, not from the controller's own pods.
ingress.controllerUnread: The pods of controller {{controller}} cannot be read.
ingress.controllerNotReady_one: Controller {{controller}} has {{count}} pod, and it is not Ready.
ingress.controllerNotReady_other: Controller {{controller}} has {{count}} pods, and none is Ready.
ingress.controllerNotFound: No pod labelled {{selector}} was found for controller {{controller}}, but the Ingress has an address: the controller may be installed with other labels.
ingress.controllerNone: No pod of controller {{controller}} runs (looked for pods labelled {{selector}}), and the Ingress has no address.
ingress.noAddress: The Ingress has no address yet. Some controllers never publish one; others do once they handle the Ingress.
ingress.tlsNoSecret: A TLS entry for {{hosts}} names no Secret: the controller's default certificate is used.
ingress.tlsUnknown: The certificate in Secret {{name}} could not be read.
ingress.tlsForbidden: Secret {{name}} cannot be read with your permissions, so its certificate is not checked.
ingress.tlsSecretMissing: Secret {{name}} does not exist in namespace {{namespace}}, or it holds no tls.crt.
ingress.tlsInvalid: Secret {{name}} holds no certificate that can be read.
ingress.tlsExpired: The certificate in Secret {{name}} has expired.
ingress.tlsNotYetValid: The certificate in Secret {{name}} is not valid yet.
ingress.tlsNoHosts: A TLS entry with Secret {{name}} names no hosts: which hosts it serves is up to the controller.
ingress.tlsHostNotCovered: The certificate in Secret {{name}} does not cover {{hosts}}: clients reject the connection. It covers: {{names}}.
ingress.tlsOk: The certificate in Secret {{name}} is valid and covers {{hosts}}.
ingress.tlsCommonNameOnly: The certificate has no DNS names, only a common name; current clients ignore the common name.
ingress.noRules: The Ingress has neither rules nor a default backend: it sends traffic nowhere.
ingress.ruleNoPaths: The rule for host {{host}} has no paths: its requests go to the controller's default backend.
ingress.pathImplementationSpecific: pathType ImplementationSpecific: how {{path}} matches is up to the controller (for some, a regular expression).
ingress.pathInvalid: Path {{path}} does not start with /: no request can match it.
ingress.pathExact: pathType Exact: only requests for exactly {{path}} match.
ingress.pathPrefix: pathType Prefix: {{path}} and everything below it match, element by element ({{path}}/a matches, {{path}}a does not).
ingress.pathEverything: pathType Prefix with /: every request for the host matches.
ingress.prefixRegex: Path {{path}} looks like a regular expression, but pathType Prefix compares path elements literally.
ingress.resourceBackend: The backend is {{kind}} {{name}}, not a Service; Sextant does not follow it.
ingress.backendNoPort: The backend Service {{name}} names no port.
ingress.servicesUnknown: The Services of namespace {{namespace}} cannot be read.
ingress.serviceMissing: Service {{name}} does not exist in namespace {{namespace}}: the controller answers 503 or 404.

route.noParents: The route names no parent Gateway in spec.parentRefs: nothing sends traffic to it.
route.parentOther: The route attaches to {{kind}} {{name}}, which is not a Gateway; Sextant does not follow it.
route.gatewayMissing: Gateway {{name}} does not exist in namespace {{namespace}}.
route.parentRejected: Gateway {{name}} did not accept the route ({{reason}}).
route.parentPending: No controller has reported on the route for Gateway {{name}} yet.
route.parentAccepted: Gateway {{name}} accepted the route on listeners: {{listeners}}.
route.gatewayNoAddress: The Gateway has no address yet.
route.gatewayProblem: Gateway {{name}} accepted the route, but it is not working itself ({{reason}}).
route.ruleNoBackends: The rule has no backends: matching requests get a 500 response.
route.ruleRedirect: The rule redirects its requests, so it needs no backend.
route.weightZero: The backend's weight is 0: it gets no share of the traffic.
route.backendNotService: The backend is {{kind}} {{name}}, not a Service; Sextant does not follow it.
route.backendNoPort: The backend Service {{name}} names no port: a Service backend needs one.
route.servicesUnknown: The Services of namespace {{namespace}} cannot be read.

policies.unreadable: The network policies cannot be read, so whether traffic from {{source}} gets in is not known.
policies.notIsolated: No network policy isolates the pods for ingress: traffic from {{source}} gets in.
policies.allowed: Network policies isolate the pods for ingress, and a rule lets traffic from {{source}} in.
policies.denied: Network policies deny traffic from {{source}} to the pods.
policies.partial_one: Network policies let traffic from {{source}} in to {{count}} pod of {{total}} and deny it to the others.
policies.partial_other: Network policies let traffic from {{source}} in to {{count}} pods of {{total}} and deny it to the others.
policies.unknown: Whether network policies let traffic from {{source}} in cannot be told from the objects.
policies.dependsOnSource: Network policies isolate the pods for ingress; whether traffic from {{source}} gets in depends on which client it is.
policies.enforcement: Network policies have an effect only when the cluster's network plugin enforces them.
policies.egressNotChecked: The controller's own egress policies are not checked.
policies.isolatedBy: Isolated by: {{policies}}; no rule of them matches.

contour.orphaned: No root HTTPProxy includes {{name}}, so Contour ignores it.
contour.orphanedWhy: A proxy without a virtualhost is served only through a root proxy that includes it (spec.includes).
contour.pending: No Contour has processed HTTPProxy {{name}} yet: Contour is not running, or the proxy belongs to another Contour.
contour.pendingClass: No Contour has processed HTTPProxy {{name}} yet: Contour is not running, or no Contour serves the ingress class {{class}}.
contour.invalidInPart: Contour serves HTTPProxy {{name}} in part ({{reason}}): the failing parts are found below.
contour.rootNamespaces: Contour accepts root proxies only in the namespaces of its --root-namespaces flag, which Sextant cannot see.
contour.hostNoAddress: Contour serves the host {{fqdn}}, but reports no address for it yet.
contour.hostNoAddressWhy: Contour copies the address of its Envoy Service; check that Service's load balancer.
contour.tlsPassthrough: TLS is passed through to the backend unopened: the backend holds the certificate.
contour.tlsNoSecret: The virtualhost has TLS but names no secretName.
contour.delegationNotServed: The TLS Secret is in namespace {{namespace}}, but the cluster does not serve TLSCertificateDelegation.
contour.delegationUnknown: The TLSCertificateDelegations of namespace {{namespace}} cannot be read.
contour.delegationMissing: Secret {{name}} is in namespace {{namespace}}, and no TLSCertificateDelegation there lets namespace {{target}} use it: Contour refuses it (DelegationNotPermitted).
contour.delegation: A TLSCertificateDelegation lets this namespace use Secret {{name}} of namespace {{namespace}}.
contour.mirror: A mirror: it gets a copy of {{percent}}% of the requests, and its answers are dropped.
contour.shareZero: Service {{name}} gets no requests: other services of the route have a weight and it has none.
contour.serviceMissing: Service {{name}} does not exist in namespace {{namespace}}: Contour leaves it out of the route (ServiceUnresolvedReference). Contour looks for Services only in the proxy's own namespace.
contour.externalName: Contour refuses ExternalName Services unless it is started with enableExternalNameService, which Sextant cannot see.
contour.service: The route sends to Service {{name}}, port {{port}}.
contour.routeRedirect: The route redirects its requests, so it needs no service.
contour.routeDirect: The route answers {{code}} itself, so it needs no service.
contour.routeNoService: The route has no service other than a mirror: Contour answers its requests with 503.
contour.proxiesUnknown: The HTTPProxies of namespace {{namespace}} cannot be read here.
contour.includeMissing: HTTPProxy {{name}} does not exist in namespace {{namespace}}: Contour answers the included paths with 502 (IncludeNotFound).
contour.includeCycle: Including {{name}} again makes a cycle: Contour refuses it (IncludeCreatesCycle).
contour.includeRoot: {{name}} is a root proxy, and a root cannot be included: Contour answers the included paths with 502 (RootIncludesRoot).
contour.deeper: The includes of {{name}} go deeper than Sextant follows here; open it to diagnose it.
contour.included: The proxy has no virtualhost: its routes are served under the host of the root proxies that include it, after their prefixes.

openshift.pending: No router has answered for the Route yet.
openshift.notAdmitted: No router has admitted the Route: no router runs, or no router's shard selects it.
openshift.notAdmittedWhy: A router serves only the Routes its route and namespace selectors pick (the IngressController's routeSelector and namespaceSelector).
openshift.noHost: The Route has no host yet.
openshift.tlsNone: No TLS: the Route serves plain HTTP.
openshift.insecureRedirect: Plain HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.
openshift.insecureAllow: Plain HTTP is served as well.
openshift.tlsPassthrough: TLS is passed through to the pods unopened: the pods hold the certificate.
openshift.tlsExternal: The certificate comes from Secret {{name}}; Sextant does not read it here.
openshift.tlsRouterCertificate: The Route sets no certificate: the router's default certificate is served.
openshift.tlsNoKey: The Route sets a certificate but no private key.
openshift.tlsServiceCa: No destination CA certificate: the router trusts the service CA for the connection to the pods.
openshift.tlsEdge: TLS ends at the router; it sends plain HTTP to the pods.
openshift.tlsReencrypt: TLS ends at the router, which opens a new TLS connection to the pods.
openshift.tlsUnknown: The TLS termination {{termination}} is not one OpenShift knows.
openshift.notService: The backend is {{kind}} {{name}}, not a Service: the router sends nothing to it.
openshift.allWeightsZero: Every backend's weight is 0: the router answers 503.
openshift.weightZero: Service {{name}} has weight 0: it gets no requests.
openshift.serviceMissing: Service {{name}} does not exist in namespace {{namespace}}: the router answers 503. A Route sends only to Services of its own namespace.
openshift.namedTargetUnknown: Target port {{port}} may be the pod port a named target port of Service {{name}} leads to; Sextant cannot tell which.
openshift.noNamedPort: Service {{name}} has no port named {{port}} (its ports: {{ports}}): the router has no endpoint to send to.
openshift.noTargetPort: No port of Service {{name}} targets pod port {{port}} (its ports: {{ports}}): the router has no endpoint to send to.
openshift.everyPort: Without a target port the router sends to every port of the Service ({{ports}}); the checks below follow the first.
openshift.service: The Route sends to Service {{name}}, port {{port}}.
